title: Taking the Bus and the LRT
title_es: Moverte en camión y en LRT
intro_es: No necesitas coche para moverte por Edmonton: aprende a usar el transporte público como local.
paragraphs: Edmonton is a big city, but you don't need a car to move around. Edmonton Transit Service, usually called ETS, has buses all over the city and a train system called the LRT, which means Light Rail Transit. The LRT is fast and goes to downtown, the university and other busy areas. Buses connect the neighbourhoods to the train stations.

Before your first trip, plan your route. You can use a map app or the ETS website to see which bus to take and when it arrives. Many bus stops have a number on the sign. Write it down, because it helps you check the schedule. In winter, try to arrive a few minutes early, but don't wait outside too long when it is very cold.

To pay your fare, you can use Arc, the reloadable fare card for the Edmonton area. You tap the card on the reader when you get on the bus or before you go to the train platform. You can add money or a monthly pass online or at some stations. Keep your card in an easy pocket so you don't hold up the line.

Being polite on transit is important in Canada. Let people get off before you get on. Offer the priority seats near the front to older people, pregnant women and people with disabilities. Take off your backpack when the bus is full, and use headphones for music or videos. Many people in Edmonton say “thank you” to the driver when they leave the bus.
If you are not sure where to get off, ask the driver or another passenger: “Excuse me, does this bus go to the hospital?” Most people are happy to help. After a few trips, you will feel like a local.
